title: The main Buddhist tree.
body: Bodhi is called banyan in Russian. In Buddhism, this tree has sacred meaning and is found in every monastery. The high status is due to the fact that it was under it that Gautama attained enlightenment in Bodh Gaya. However, that tree did not survive, but from its seed was grown a tree in Anuradhapura in the time of King Ashoka. It is pointless to argue over the sacred status of this tree, for it is the truth of faith, not the truth of reason. But the fact that this tree has the longest documented history in the world is highly probable. 2,300 years! What's more, the sprouts of this ficus have been taken to Buddhist monasteries all over the world! True, if you look closely, you'll see that the tree is not one, but several. Besides, the oldest one won't let you in, it's upstairs behind the fence.

body: This sacred tree, grown from a sapling of the original Bodhi Tree in Bodhgaya India and brought here by Asoka's daughter Sanghamitta in the 3rd century BC, is of enormous significance to Buddhists from all over the world. This is a central and very sacred place of pilgrimage and the atmosphere is very special, especially so during daily puja's and poya days. Namo Buddhaya, Budu Saranai, Theruwan Saranai.May all beings be happy and well.

title: Oldest tree in the world
body: The Sri Lankans claim this buddhist bodhi tree is the oldest tree in the world. It is certainly sacred and the site of religious pilgrimage for Buddhists. Tourists should go quietly and respectfully. You will also notice extensive security the result of Tamil attacks in the 90's.

title: Not the oldest tree in the world
body: Came here thinking that. It's actually the oldest and living human-planted tree in the world. The tree looks old no doubt but it looks like any other Bo tree you can find in Sri Lanka.

title: Special place

title: Really old

title: Sacred Tree

title: A sacred tree supported in golden poles
body: From the LP guidebook description I was not expecting much, but I was pleasantly surprised by the way this tree has been preserved, and protected. It stands on a tiered platform, which has been built up over the centuries to support the branches as the tree has developed. Only two branches of the original tree remain: one old original, supported on magnificent golden poles, and one relatively new shoot. It is also surrounded by 'daughter' trees.

title: The oldest tree in the world
body: The original Bodh tree looks a little sick, but its offspring that is surrounding him looks much better. Definetely a very holy place and a must-do when you are interested in the culture of Sri Lanka

title: This tree is more than 2000 yrs old! Great spectacle and welcome blessing.

That level of loving nourishment and care is remarkable in itself, but it is the devotees who really make this site an interesting spectacle. The pilgrims had travelled from as far as Thailand to see the Maha Bodhi tree and to be blessed. We felt privileged to receive a blessing here, too.

title: Essential part of the trip

title: AN ODD HISTORICAL STRUCTURE
body: There is little so see today of the Brazen Palace. Made of wood, it burnt down several times over the centuries. It may have been a monastic, rather than royal, residence. There are more than a few doubts about the reputed 9 stories, yet alone 1,000 rooms. Some of the pillars presently standing are not original. With some background, a traveler can imagine past grandeur while a tourist will just pass by muttering.

title: Quite disappointing

title: A one minute photographic opportunity
body: We're sure that the 'Brazen Palace' will have been quite a spectacle in its day - but the reality now - is 1,600 unornate fenced off columns. Worth a quick photo if you're passing it on the way to the sacred bodhi tree but not worth going out of your way (in our opinion).

title: Interesting architecturally
body: Lovamahapaya is otherwise known as Brazen Place because of the bronze tiles that were used on its roof. It is of interest to those fascinated by the architecture and construction techniques of ancient times and adds to the amazing variety of cultural highlights to be found in the Anuradhapura area. Today Lovamahapaya is rather dilapidated but one can appreciate the magnificence of the original building with its 1,600 stone pillars.

title: Impressive History
body: The fenced off 1600 pillars are all that remains of what was once a palace of great heights. It's impressive to look at them and think that they are more than 2000 years old.

title: Another Place of Worship by the Buddhist
body: This too is located in Anuradhapura close to Sri Maha Bodhi and Ruwanwelisaya. This was used as a place to get the Buddhist Monks assembled on “Poya” days to recite the “Pirith”. According to history this was a nine story building done by King “Dutugemunu” who built the “Ruwanwelisya”.

title: Wonderful photo opps! Wear flip flops
body: Best advice: wear flip flops or other inexpensive sandals because you must remove your shoes to enter these holy places. Don't wear sneakers because they are difficult to take off quickly and when it rains, they are quite uncomfortable. Beware the men trying to sell trinkets; don't show any interest, or they will follow you around for your entire visit and beg you to buy their goods. They will not leave you alone, and there are no tourist police to report them.

title: Amazing night tour
body: We were so lucky to be with Poorna on the night tour. We saw two lorris, including one capturing and eating a butterfly. We also saw a brown wood owl and a spotted mouse deer. What an amazing experience!

title: Good tour
body: Great night tour by Poorna to see the wild Loris - we even saw a baby! We also walked around before it got dark and saw a Giant Squirrel. Very good

title: Loris watching
body: We went late afternoon for Loris watching and wow was it worth it ! We were welcomed with a cup of tea and a very warm welcome of the tame baby owl who was very sweet. Poorna the enthusiastic arboretum specialist gave us first a very interesting explanation about the arboretum and Loris, his knowledge is amazing! We then went out to find the Loris as soon as it was dark, Poorna gave us head torches and we saw 3 Loris and a baby Loris within 20minutes!We can highly recommend a visit !

title: Wonderfull
body: Held by nature enthusiasts, this place is ideal for a beautiful walk in the middle of various trees and plants.

title: Amazing Visit
body: We visited in February this year and had a wonderful time. Mr Amarasinghe took us round, explaining in depth about the various flora and fauna. We wanted to do a night walk, but unfortunately were limited on time. We were very fortunate to see a mouse deer in the daytime, which is uncommon apparently. Would definitely recommend visiting, it's a very unique experience that needs tourist support. We would love to come back to Sri Lanka one day, and will definitely return and hopefully do a night walk!

title: Best part of our Sri Lanka trip
body: Please please go visit this wonderful place. We went twice, once during the day and once for a night tour to see the Loris - and we did!!!! Mr Jayarantha went with us both times and we have become great friends. Thank you Mr. Jayarantha!!! And thank you Mr. Popham.

title: Popham Arboretum, Dambulla.
body: We spent a thoroughly interesting two hours with Jayantha, learning about the various indigenous trees and their uses, as well as learning something of the history of the arboretum. A real national treasure.This place is certainly worth a visit if you are interested in the natural world.

title: Always nice to come here
body: Dropped by Sam Popham Arboretum, Sri Lanka last weekend. Filled the vehicle with sapling...excellent selection. Got some hard-to-find Gal siyambala, Weera, Kora Kaha, Burutha, Kaha Pethan, Bata Kirilla as well as the more popular Ehala, Welang, Hal milla...See you next time!

title: Great time at the Popham Arboretum- Loris Included!
body: I visited in September 2016 with some friends from the Colombo area. We had a great time. The manager was very friendly, and took us on a few hikes through the arboretum. My favorite was a nighttime safari, during which I spotted a loris! Definitely a high point of my trip. Yes, the facilities are rustic, but that's the point! It's a great feeling getting away from the hustle and bustle of the city and enjoying the natural world. I would recommend this place to anyone who is looking for a rustic getaway in a beautiful natural setting.

title: Nice Place to Camping

title: A piece of historic Sri Lankan engineering ingenuity

title: Still worth a visit
body: The twin baths are yet another testament to the once upon a time grandeur of one of Sri Lanka's native kingdoms. I have to admit that before visiting Anuradhapura, I was not aware that Sri Lanka had such a long and rich history, that it had a civilization that was complex and advanced enough to rival that anywhere else. The whole time I was staring at the twin baths, I kept thinking "How could the people have afforded to build these back then? Where was the source of their wealth?" The twin baths, after all, are very big, especially for just two people. It can thus be looked at as either a symbol of wealth and power and/or waste and frivolous spending. Regardless, the twin baths are definitely worth a look, simply because they are so well preserved, even after a thousand years, unlike many of the other relics in and around Anuradhapura. Just be careful not to fall in! The water is indeed very green!

Old machinery can be seen and a range of artefacts from the early period of tea production under British control. Quite interesting but not exciting. There is a range of small units selling tea on the upper floor and a small tea bar on the top floor.

title: excellent intro to the history of tea in England
body: before this visit, i knew absolutely nothing about tea. I'm a coffee drinker. Who know that pekoe is the size of the tea flakes after they are ground? This place runs thru the entire process from picking thru sorting/packaging. there is a tea tasting, a good video, and interesting old machines.

title: Go and have a cuppa
body: Enjoyed this tour and learned more about tea and the quality of it. Nice complimentary tea too, very enjoyable couple of hours with fellow backpackers.

title: Go and have a cuppa
body: Enjoyed this tour and learned more about tea and the quality of it. Nice complimentary tea too, very enjoyable couple of hours with fellow backpackers.

title: Interesting tour
body: Was more interesting than I had anticipated. I learned quite a lot about the production of tea in Sri Lanka. It is worth a visit.

title: Nice place
body: Its worth watching .you may have the knowledge of tea history. And how we done this nice work. from that place you can by tea.

title: Worth stopping
body: Very interesting to see how the tea is processed from the time picked from the plants until is bagged and sent to auction.

title: it's what Ceylon about.

title: Good place to tea loves.
body: this place is actually important for tea loves because you can learn many things about tea and you can see the old machinery when British period they were used .

title: love the history
body: It was a lovely experience to get the knowledge of the inception of tea. They could actually improve the standards to make the tour more worthwhile. It was a very educational experience.

title: Go and take a look you will not be disappointed
body: Wow this place is brilliant - heaped in history you simply must go and visit.You will find out everything there is to know about tea - remember it used to be called Ceylon!!!

title: TEA EXPERIENCE
body: Excellent selection of teas that tea lovers would enjoy anytime, and would never forget! Recommended for every visitor to Sri Lanka

title: Only if you are interested in tea
body: It was nothing special only the different variety of teas that are offered for sale is a good deal, but the tour was ok.

title: INSPIRING

title: Great visit, very interesting

title: Tea factory
body: Tea factory.. you can get to see and know the processes involved before tea becomes final product. They have variety tea bags with different flavors for sale.

title: NOT QUITE WHAT WE EXPECTED
body: Worth a visit but we were expecting to see the plantation, pickers etc. This felt like a tourist location to earn money. If you have never been then of course go, drink and buy the tea.

title: Ceylon Tea at its best
body: An interesting insight into how tea is grown and processed. It is back breaking work picking the tea on the mountainsides, and most of it is done by Tamil women imported from India.Bought some prime grade Ceylon tea to give as presents on my return home.

title: Interesting, no more Tea Bags
body: This was really interesting and the tea taste at the end was good, can't believe there are so many different types and the processes they go through. Don't have tea bags as it's just the dust would you believe.

title: Marwalas.
body: Visiters can see old glory of worlds best tea (ceylon tea) manufacters machinares & what metherd they used in those days.to keep up the grate quality of ceylon tea.

title: educational

title: Very Interesting
body: Spent about an hour at The Mackwoods Plantation and it brought back school day memories of learning about where tea comes from!Very interesting to go into the factory where the smell of tea was quite overpowering-glad I don't have to work there!Most of the pickets are still women and still get paid according to how much they pickWorth a vist

title: Variety of Tea
body: you visit this place and you get to know the various ways and means in which the superb Sri Lankan tea is made.....We just loved it. we also purchased good amount of tea variety from there.

title: Real Ceylon Tea

title: Discovering the History of the Cup of Tea

title: I hate tea but I liked the factory

title: Do not miss it, very interesting

title: Well worth the climb!

Followed route listed on the blog ‘atlas and boots’ - would recommend using that!A few places selling drinks along the way but would recommend taking water, snacks and some wipes with you. You don’t need fancy walking shoes, trainers are fine but watch for the slippy ground on the final steep incline. The fresh juice stands at the top we’re most welcome! For the average fairly fit person I would say the climb is moderate!

title: Nice and confusing walk
body: Confusing as expected, but eventually made it to the top. Don't worry too much because you will see a lot of people as confused as you, just enjoy the adventure!

title: Ashok Vatika
body: Visited here on Jan 23rd,2019. As per folklore, the Sri Lankan demon King Ravana after abducting Sita, kept her hidden in this area and this area was offered to Sita as a pleasure garden, the place finds mention in the Ramayana as Ashok Vatika. This place is of special cultural significance to Indians!

title: Visit to Hakgala Gardens
body: A walk in the park is the best you could do in this area; it is 68 acres in area and established during the British regime in 1838. We used a Golf Cart to accomplish to cover the area.

title: Brilliant for nature lovers
body: As the park is big and we had limited time, we chose to do the tour with the large 6 seater buggy. We were fortunate that our driver had an intricate knowledge of the history , plants and trees.There is so much to see and nature lovers could spend days exploring this wonderful garden

title: must visit

title: Beautiful Park

title: Variety of green
body: Great place to spend a day. But we had to wait for more than an hour for the golf car to come around for us.

title: Nice botanical garden,I love this

title: Lovely Botanical Garden

title: Awesome++ botanical garden

title: FANTASTIC GARDEN

title: Lovely Place
body: Beautiful Place surrounded with no. of flowers and trees of different kinds and have about 4 different zones .

title: Very very beautiful and mesmerising for all plant lovers
body: It is an extremely beautiful garden that is situated on a height. If you love spending time with flowers and greenery then this is the place you must visit. But try and go there during flower season time. In May, there are fewer flowers but they are still there. Can be difficult for senior citizens to go upto the garden as its on a slope that you need to climb up and on your way down. Thought I have seen a golf cart there which is available on chargeable basis. But the drop off point seems to be upstairs only near exit point. So people who have difficulty in walking may find it a bit challenging navigating their way up and down. Otherwise its a great place to visit and spend time.

title: We enjoyed seeing the monkeys
body: There was a lot of greenery but not many flowers in bloom. The highlight of our viit were the monkeys an the top of the gardens

title: They need to manage more
body: Visited in the April season. But still, they are planting some areas. So there are no much flowers. Management has to target the season.

title: Do not visit during March/April
body: If you are planning to visit srilanka in march then i would suggest to skip this place as march is the season when they plant new flowers. so there wont be much to see during that time. Also you can find a board outside displaying the same, I would suggest to visit pinnawala botanical garden instead

title: Attractive hillside gardens
body: We realised that the best displays of annuals would be in April but there was still lots to enjoy, especially the extensive hillside fernery and the general ambience.

title: Worth a visit
body: Extremely well laid out with a variety of themes all presented in a very natural setting. Our visit did not give us the best of the gardens because of the time of year i.e February. We expect that the gardens would be best viewed between May and July and September to November to really get an appreciation of the variety of plants and flowers in bloom

title: Very interesting place with so much Nature.
body: Visit the location just because it was recommended by friends. As i Arrived, my imagination changed with all these different types of trees and flower gardens available. title: Good experience

title: Rose garden is very beautiful

title: Nice Place

title: Garden with beautiful flowers

title: Beautiful!
body: Thoroughly enjoyed getting close to nature at this botanical garden. It's not as large as the Peradeniya gardens in Kandy but it is beautiful. Yes, it's not as much fun as walking around, but the drivers are quite knowledgeable and will tell you little fascinating tidbits of info. We had a lovely driver, Herath, who regaled us with facts about lots of plants which my son found quite interesting.

title: Cozy , medium size botanic heaven

title: Amazing place

title: Good

title: Excellent

title: Beautiful gardens

title: Nice Garden

title: Nice place to visit.

title: Hakgla Botnical garden is a our one of the main Resource.

title: Highest set botanical gardens in the world
body: Hakgala Botanical Garden is one of the three botanical gardens in Sri Lana. The other two being Peradeniya Botanical Garden and Henarathgoda Botanical Garden. It is the second largest garden in Sri Lanka. The garden is contiguous to Hakgala Strict Nature Reserve in Nuwara Eliya. The gardens is believed to be the highest set botanical gardens in the world.Hakgala Gardens is open daily from 8.00 am to 5.30 pm. Plant nursery closes at 3.00 pm. Wheel chairs are available for hire at a nominal rent. Although light motor vehicles are permitted to enter the gardens, visitors are advised to walk around Hakgala gardens if they wish to explore the many beautiful places in this very compact garden.We spent a good 4 hours at the garden and enjoyed every bit of it and also bought plants from the nursery. Please note that the plant nursery closes at 3.30 pm. The garden is open on all days from 8.00 am to 5.30 pm.

title: Waste of Time !!
body: One of the reasons we went to Sri Lanka was to see a tea factory in production. Owing to the type of tea they produce here the production only takes place at night. We were given a quick tour around looking at inactive machines which made us none the wiser. You are then left in the reception area to watch a marketing video about how wonderful Pedro is and how they are helping the community etc (and given a cup of tea!). Given the lack of tea production you see on this waste of time tour, it would be far more useful to show a video of the tea production, at least then you would not feel you were leaving as badly informed as you were when you arrived! There are tea factories where you can see tea being produced and I suggest you visit one of those!!

title: Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya - A Tropical Paradise in the Heart of Sri Lanka
body: What Makes It SpecialThe Avenue of Royal Palms - Perhaps the most photographed spot in the gardens, this stunning avenue features towering double rows of royal palms planted in 1905. Walking beneath these majestic giants creates an unforgettable experience.The Orchid House - Home to over 300 varieties of orchids, this climate-controlled greenhouse displays some of the most exotic and rare orchid species in the world, with year-round blooming varieties.Giant Javan Fig Tree - One of the garden's most impressive attractions, this enormous tree on the great lawn covers an area of over 2,500 square meters. It's perfect for a shaded picnic or rest.The Spice Garden - Discover cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, and other spices that made Sri Lanka famous along ancient trade routes.Memorial Trees Famous personalities including King George V, Queen Elizabeth II, Yuri Gagarin, and Emperor Haile Selassie have planted commemorative trees here, adding historical significance to your visit.

title: Expansive and stunning, this botanical garden boasts a vast, diverse collection of plants
body: We visited the Royal Botanical Gardens in Kandy, a sprawling 147-acre expanse that dates back to the 14th century, though its formal establishment was in 1821. We only had time to explore a small portion, perhaps two or three acres, but were captivated by its beauty. The gardens are world-renowned for their extensive collection of over 4,000 plant species, including a magnificent orchid house, spices, medicinal plants, and imposing palm avenues. A unique feature is the tradition of visiting dignitaries planting memorial trees; one notable example is the Ceylon ironwood tree planted by Tsar Nicholas II of Russia during his visit in 1891.

title: It's a must in Kandy!

title: Relaxing excursion
body: Great excursion. Very relaxing and interesting tour - saw a lot in an hour. Lots of different specimens and some lovely landscaping.

title: One of the most interesting Botanic Gardens I ever saw- needed more time
body: I was so impressed at every turn. This is a place not be missed. There are so many exotic species, endemic , native, and toxic species all color coded. I found wandering the outside regions instead of the orchid house more interesting personally. They had a large collection of cacti and succulents and incredible old huge trees. AN umbrella or at least a sun hat was important when we went. We had a trolley drive and stop so that we were able to cover more of the park. This is a wonderful place to spend several hours.

title: Not to be missed
body: It's a real joy to have this breath of oxygen and greenery after the tumult of Kandi. Not the most flowery period but the trees are exceptional

title: We spent 2 enjoyable hours here
body: We spent 2 hours here on the way from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya, enjoyed it very much and would recommend a visit. Be prepared though for not much information in english or labelling of the plants and trees

title: Not worth paying to visit but may be included in your trip
body: Extensive botanical gardens which seem well frequented by Sri Lankans.While covering a significant area, this is not as impressive as Botanical Gardens in other global locations (and probably influenced a lot by climate).We visited as part of a Sri Lanka Tour (and to pass time before something else).

title: A highlight in Kandy
body: A true oasis and escape from the businesses of the city. The gardens are well cared for a lovely way to while away around three hours in leafy greenness. Many notable and interesting plants and trees.

title: refreshing mind
body: An amazing place close to the bustling city. We spent 2 hours there, refreshing both mind and body. Beautiful plants and greenhouses. We fed little monkeys that run freely in the garden and enjoyed the shade of the trees. We walked through the entire park on foot, but saw that you can also rent golf carts.

title: Another visit to the excellent gardens
body: Every time we go anywhere near Kandy we visit the Royal Botanical Gardens at Peradeniya and spend an hour walking through them. As usual and as expected, they were excellent.

title: Expected more for Rs3000
body: Ripping off the tourists as it is the norm everywhere in SL. Not worth Rs3000 but good vfm for the locals. Wouldn't recommend

title: SRI Lanka tour
body: This was a really good trip if you are interested in gardens and trees. The gardens are massive, but there are some amazing trees to see, some planted by very famous people

title: a Simple garden
body: This Garden was huge with lots of plants and tree but it was not as i expected from a Royal Garden. it was not a real organized Royal Garden

title: Worth visiting, but overall a little disappointing.
body: This is Sri Lanka's main botanical gardens; as such we expected more (especially having see the equivalent in other Asian countries such as Singapore).Sri Lanka has a vast range of "exotic" plants native to the country - thus you would expect the botanical gardens to display them to the full - put simply, it doesn't.Well worth visiting, and well looked after.

title: Beautiful walk through Royal Botanical Gardens
body: Beautifully kept, very well laid out gardens with many species of trees, plants, shrubs and grasses. Giant Bamboos, many varieties of palms, huge trees. Tree lined avenues and riverside walk. Nice way to enjoy 2hrs relaxing in the open air.

title: Gagarin planted a tree here
body: I'm not a botany buff, but the garden amazed me. Be sure to check out two trees planted by our compatriots - Gagarin and Nicholas I.

title: Excellent botanical garden
body: Excellent experience. Wide range of plants, trees and orchids. There are monuments inside the garden. Superb experience.

title: Very beautiful botanical garden
body: I really enjoyed visiting this place. Lots of beautiful trees and other plants. Take water, you will definitely spend one or two hours there. If you love nature, this is the place for you.

title: Average
body: There are better botanical displays elsewhere in the world. Even Kew Gardens in the UK is better. It’s a shame really as they have a good climate here for things to flourish well. It’s something to do whilst in Kandy, but I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone coming to Sri Lanka.

title: Worth a visit!
body: Really nice experience.We only had 1 and a half hour, that wasnt enough. My guess is that you need 3-4 hours of your want to see everything and maybe also have a little break.Very pretty and impressive

title: Top thing to do in Kandy
body: This botanical garden houses rare doule coconut trees, fragrant orchid collection, palm way and spice garden to name a few. We spent almost 3-4 hours at this spot.

title: Royal Botanical Gardens
body: This about 3 miles west of Kandy. It has many plants and many orchids and palm trees. The National Herbarium is attached. It goes back to 1371 under King Wickramananu

title: So so
body: Botanical Gardens outside Kandy.Not very well looked after, very large and with lots of plants.Worth a visit if you have time to spare.

title: Amazing place
body: Nice place for walking and for those who are addicted to the nature.We spend 3 hours there and the place was amazing

title: Inspiring
body: Amazing. Equal to, if not better than Singapore botanical gardens. Great collection. Nearly all plants have a plaque to explain origin, name etc. Beautifully maintained. Definitely worth the time and effort to stroll around

title: So so
body: Botanical Gardens outside Kandy.Not very well looked after, very large and with lots of plants.Worth a visit if you have time to spare.

title: Amazing place
body: Nice place for walking and for those who are addicted to the nature.We spend 3 hours there and the place was amazing

title: Inspiring
body: Amazing. Equal to, if not better than Singapore botanical gardens. Great collection. Nearly all plants have a plaque to explain origin, name etc. Beautifully maintained. Definitely worth the time and effort to stroll around

title: Beautiful and very relaxing
body: I recently visited the Royal Botanical Gardens. What a great experience w. The gardens are extensive and was so relaxing to walk around.

title: Absolutely loved this place!
body: We stopped for a quick visit on our way to Nuwara Eliya but ended up staying for two hours in there because it is so beautiful and enormous. It is very relaxing to walk around or sit for a picnic. Huge collection of plants from all over the world and large trees that are more than 50 years old. Highly recommended if you are staying in Kandy or just passing by!

title: Most nice place in Kandy
body: Actually in Kandy no more places to visit, this Park is the main place in the to, so if you are tourist you have to visit it. It has all kind of plan

title: Beautiful
body: Amazing to see all the different types of trees and plants. Nice walk, plenty of shade to keep you cool

title: A must-do in Kandy
body: If you're travelling to Kandy, visiting these gardens is a must. They are beautiful. A nature-lovers dream.

title: Elegantly Landscaped Garden
body: Peradeniya Royal Botanical Garden is a must-visit place in Kandy. It is an elegantly landscaped garden with palm tree avenues, pine avenues, and flower beds. The Orchid House is quite beautiful with lots of colorful blooms.

title: Good walking tour
body: Had a good walk through the gardens. There are several unique plants in the garden. The orchids were OK but there were not as many that I heard about.

title: Awesome botanical garden!
body: You can easily spend the half day there. The exhibition has a high variety of local and global plants. We absolutely recommend to go there if you have time.

title: Very impressive gardens
body: Went to the gardens with mixed emotions, wasn't too sure I would enjoy it. Wow was I surprised. They are stunning with loads to see. Loved Royal Palm avenue, loved watching the bats flying around in the large fir trees and the orchids were magnificent. Well worth a visit

title: Fantastic gardens
body: Beautiful gardens and extensive grounds all immaculately kept .Easy to follow route around main sights and we particularly enjoyed the beautiful orchid house.

title: What a fantastic garden
body: Go and visit this amazing garden if you can. Plants trees orchids palms cycads they are all here to enchant and educate

title: Loved it! Way beyond our expectations
body: Am not one for mancured lawns, etc. But this was very impressive! Orginally designed and run by British gardeners, now under Sri Lankan management, of course, and quite lovely!

title: Gorgeous Gardens
body: One of our favourite stops during our visit to Sri Lanka, these historic gardens are impressive, and beautifully maintained.Featuring trees, plants and flowers from all over the world, it is a testament to the curiosity of British settlers who first established them (and the to sustained commitment of the Sri Lankan government to preserving the site.Lovely grounds to stroll, with many spots providing cooling shade to escape the often oppressive heat. We spent a few hours roaming, and saw perhaps half of the park. The orchid house is s highlight, as are the tree-lined pathways featuring particular species (double coconuts, royal palms, etc).

title: Magnificent gardens
body: It's really worth visiting these gardens and don't skimp on time as there's a lot to see. It's beautifully laid out and well signposted.

title: Beautiful Gardens
body: This is a must see in Kandy.There is a big variety of plants and what impressed me the most was that not only is the names of the plants/trees shown, but also the country of origin. We spend about 3 hours there but if you have time you can spend the whole day.The layout is also good and interesting in some instances.

title: Beautiful and well laid out gardens
body: We loved walking through these gardens. They are beautifully landscaped with more than 4000 species of plants. They have a big collection of orchids too. The cannon ball tree was very fascinating. One can easily spend a couple of hours here without getting bored. But you have to be prepared to walk. The gardens are spread over a huge area.

title: Well worth it
body: The gardens are really worth the visit, I was shocked how much I enjoyed it. You need at least an hour

title: Pleasant day in this beautiful garden
body: We felt like we were in paradise. This garden is simply beautiful! Take your time to walk around and take in the beauty of the trees, flowers, and all sort of plants. Enjoy the peacefulness!

title: Amazing !
body: We don't want to go home after we visited the Royal Botanic Gardens. She is very impressed by the color of the flowers in the garden. She can’t stop taking pictures of her with such a lovely place. I truly loved this place.

title: Beautiful gardens and area
body: Loved our visit here especially seeing the bats hanging from the tress in one area of the gardens. Gardens are extremely well kept and beautiful to see especially the orchid house.Lots of walking to cover the vast area so recommend taking a bottle of water with you.

title: Must Go!
body: Actually "Kandy" sounds so much nicer than it is, BUT: on our second day we visited the botanical garden and it was far beyond our expections. Its a huge areal to plan at least 3 hours for the visit. Surprised by amazing garden planning and well cared...One of the best botanical gardens I ever visited.

title: An amazing place
body: These gardens are a treasure trove of tropical plants and history. They are beautifully set out and designed. The feature for many is the orchid house where some amazing orchids are on display. The avenues of trees, the lawn areas and flowering garden beds add to the general ambiance of peace and tranquility. Not to be missed in your visit to the Kandy area.

title: beautiful place
body: This is a beautiful place to have a walk. It`s not that full of tourists and is kinda quaiet to enjoy a nice day.

title: must visit place in Kandy
body: we went to the garden in the morning,very nice,so many attractive flowers had bloomed,mind relaxing place,

title: Wonderful place
body: The garden is impressive due to its size and diversity of the plants and in particular the tree-vellum fold. Definitely a place to relax and to be amazed.

title: Beautiful landscaping, rich flora, can forget the world around y
body: We love nature and taking a walk, but the Royal Botanical Garden is a 5* experience. Words don’t describe well, so see pictures

title: Kandy highlight
body: A wide range of plants many of which have been planted by dignitaries from all over the world. The orchids are spectacular. The whole area is well kept and is a great place to spend a relaxing afternoon.

title: A must visit
body: This was by far the highlight of our stay in Kandy. The gardens are stunning and there are so many plants and trees to take in. We enjoyed watching the fruit bats hanging from the trees. If you don’t have much time I would recommend prioritising the gardens.

title: Lovely Gardens
body: The gardens are huge, so there was a lot of lovely spaces to walk around and see. There were also these huge bats which were pretty cool.

title: Fabulous space
body: This garden serves as both a leisure park and a biological resource. It is popular but huge. It is located a short distance out of Kandy but travel is slow. It is largely open but there are areas of shade. Plants are largely well labelled. A good map is provided. Polythene is not permittedTh Royal Palm walk is splendid but there are many other interesting features. The orchid house is interesting and colourful. Dont miss the Javanese figs with their huge roots. Dont miss the numerous fruit bats in the northern area. There is quite a lot of birdlife too.

title: Just wow
body: You must see this place when you go to kandy , amazing, wonderful place and it was one of the places i really like, big trees with alot of roots, all kinds of tree.

title: An oasis
body: It was great to spend a few hours wandering around the gardens. There were a number of school groups at the gardens when i visited and one group took great delight in meeting me and having selfies.

title: Beautiful gardens
body: Well worth spending a couple of hours here as they are truly lovely. The orchid house is especially nice but the collections of bamboo, the herb garden but mainly the general fantastic layout of the garden. A must do while you are in Kandy

title: 147 acres of well kept gardens
body: You can cheat and spend 250rupees on taking an electric car around the main areas, but it pays to walk because you see so much more, including the large colony of flying foxes hanging from the trees. The garden is full of delights and everything is well signed in English.

title: Another excellent walk around the Royal Botanical Gardens
body: We visited the Royal Botanical Gardens with friends and thoroughly enjoyed another walk through the beautiful gardens. There is always something new to see every time we go there, including the area of trees planted by famous visitors - King Edward VII and Czar Nicholas II for example.

title: Garden is lovely but cafeteria crushed experience
body: Park is lovely and peacefull. Do not bother to order sri lankan omelette in cafeteria. U get only bland omelette with few bits of tomato. Asked about it from waitress. They just throwed me a loads of chili on different plate next to omelette. Been in Sri Lanka 1 month and this is definetly the Worst customer experience this far.

title: Wonderful Gardens
body: This is probably the most wonderful botanical garden I have visited. There is a staggering array of trees, bamboos, ferns and colourful flowers from all over the world. Even the huge grassed areas are remarkably attractive. The hundreds of fruit bats in some of the trees are spectacular to see. The orchid house is small but nevertheless very good, although it would help if there were labels identifying the various types. We spent about 2.5 hours here but would have happily spent much longer if time had allowed.

title: Such beauty and variety
body: Spent 3 hours wandering around being amazed at the variety of plants on display. Stunning orchids, enormous bamboo, medicinal plants and loads more

title: Incredible 225 year old exquisite garden !
body: Loved this place ! so absolutely beautiful.....If you like huge mature beautiful gardens and parks .....you will love this place....Lots of shade but where a hat !

title: stunning
body: large , well designed garden with beautiful collection trees and flowers. Especially the tree collection is impressing.I couldn’t see everything as my driver was waiting. Most of all it is very very well kept. next best to me with the « jardins de pamplemousse » on Mauritius.tip : go urly in the morning as it gets stickier around noon

title: Brilliant way to spend the day
body: We had such a perfect day exploring the gardens, I’d recommend it to anyone who has some spare time when visiting Kandy, so many interesting things to see, including this strange Irish man pretending to be a tree.

title: A must see
body: The botanical gardens are the largest in Sri Lanka, with huge areas of green well kept lawns. There are many different aspects to the gardens which contain specific sections such as orchids, rubber trees, the palm avenue to name a few. Giant fruit bats hang in the trees and fly screeching overhead. There's more than enough to keep you here for a few hours.

title: Beautiful
body: There are so many varieties of beautiful plants, flowers and spices. Having the monkeys around makes the experience even better. Highly Recommended.

title: interesting garden with a huge variety of plants and flowers
body: a garden with a huge variety of plants, some not even available in other parts of the world. a very enjoyable walk and the gardens even had an orchid flower house with different varieties of orchids.

title: One of the best
body: Huge grounds with the most amazing gardebs to easily walk around and enjoy. Lovely orchid house. Watch out for the trees full of bat's at one end. Everyone will enjoy this

title: Peradeniya plant conservatory
body: Visited here on Jan 21st,2019. This garden is more floral than the Hakgala botanical gardens. Plenty of couples and white skinned foreign tourists here. You can also pay extra to sit in a buggy and see the place with live commentary and photo stops by the driver - which we did here. Since it is quite large if you plan on covering it by foot/walk then plan to easily spend at least 4 hours here.

title: Visited as part of an organised trip
body: Had a great few hours here enjoying the green spaces and variety of trees and plants, could have spent a great deal more time exploring.well worth the visit

title: Wonderful gardens
body: Enjoyed a full day in these splendid gardens and still didn’t see everything. Highlights included the incredible mahoganies with their extraordinary roots, the cannonball trees whose flowers are so delicate, the talipot palm with an unusual life cycle and the gracious avenue of palms. Good buffet lunch at the canteen and a kiosk for later refreshments.

title: Large and beautiful gardens
body: These gardens are offering countless species of local exotic flora. My favorite was royal palms, memorial trees and house of orchids but that is just a tiny part of what you can run into there. Reserve few hours and about about 1500lkr for this large area that is an ideal place for walks and relax.

title: Beautiful garden - worth a visit
body: This is a very nice botanical garden, with many beautiful flowers in the garden, and a great collection of orchids. There is a pleasant relaxed atmosphere, and we could easily have spent more time there.

title: Extremely beautiful
body: This park is gorgeous! It's one of my favourite places in the world because it's extremely beautiful and very well-kept. Plus, if you enjoy being in contact with nature, I'm sure you will love spending some time here!

title: Interesting , a wide selection of trees - More Trees than Plants
body: Impressive collection of Trees from all over the World. A pleasant afternoons' diversion from the mayhem of downtown Kandy. The tree collection is quite spectacular. The Orchid House the Rose Garden etc were a little disappointing. That said I have never seen such a range of tree specimens. The Palm avenue and the Giant Bamboo trees are awesome. Well worth a visit for a couple of hours. More interesting than Kandy itself

title: Beautiful gardens - must see for nature enthusiasts
body: 200 year old royal botanic garden with a huge variety of flora and fauna to see. TIPS: thousands of bats live on the island, so if you are lucky (or loom long enough, you will definitely see and hear them. unique experience. I would suggest to plan 1.5 hrs. Garden tours on electric gold vehicles are also on offer for those who cant walk long

title: Lovely and beautiful gardens
body: Really beautiful gardens. Plenty of space to walk around and relax.Very green and lots of places to stay and enjoy the silence. We have seen many amazing specimens. We enjoyed very much the Cook's Pine Avenue.

title: Breathtaking!!!!
body: Royal Botnical Gardens in Kandy is the most beautiful place in Sri Lanka. It appears you have entred a dreamland with beautiful flowers all around. A must visit during your Sri Lanka trip

title: Great Gardens
body: Really surprising Gardens, some of the best maintained and constructed gardens....the collection of fig trees are awe inspiring!

title: Highlight is the bat colonies
body: The bat colonies here is amazing. Thousands of fruit bats hang from banyan trees. They block out the sky when they fly in herds. It's like inside a batman movie.

title: Nature
body: Great place to visit for a nature tourist. Including over 4000 plants including medicine, orchids, palm trees Etc

title: Must visit
body: This is a must visit site when in Kandy. Very relaxing garden with plenty of different types trees, flowers and other interesting plants etc. Good reserve around 2-3 hours for the visit.

title: Tourist tax strikes again!
body: Locals pay 60rpTourist pays 3000rp ($30)Very pretty inside if you like plants and trees. Lots of people and monkeys. I wouldn't go back.Try it, you might like it!

title: Loved the Botanic Gardens!
body: Definitely worth a visit. I spent a beautiful 2 hours walking around the perimeter of the gardens, so much to see and so beautifully set out.

title: Definitely a place to visit!
body: It is a place where you can spend a beatiful 3 hours and really enjoy in nature. It is meticulousy organized and well mantained. Bring a blanket to lay down on some of big lawns and relax.

title: Worth a visit
body: Pleasant walking through all the massive trees. Map was useful. Even though there was a lot of people there it still felt as if you were on your own at times which was lively

title: Very delicate and many amazing spots
body: It was more than i expected from a botanical garden! Delicate, pretty, well orgnized and definitely worth a visit！

title: Amazing
body: I love royal botanical garden at peradeniya with very beautiful greenaries around the me.very nice land of the heaven.

title: Remarkable Botanic Gardens
body: Having lived opposite Kew Gardens in London we are used to a high standard, Peradeniya was up to this standard.Well organised, an interesting selection exhibits, orchid house, fernery,bamboos, plant house and my favourite the palm avenues.Towards the end of the day, as usual, there was a thunderstorm...

title: Amazing garden
body: We could of stayed here for the rest of the day, so so much to see, we kept getting lost which we found funny, we came across a blind dog, which brought tears to our eyes. The gardens were amazing for all to see. There are so many different variety’s of plants to see here. You must not leave Sri Lanka without seeing this place.

title: Relaxing place for a stroll
body: These are beautiful gardens with a wide variety of plants. It’s a great place for a stroll with lots of shady areas to escape some of the heat.

title: Orchid
body: its a very huge place and need a one day to cover up all. i couldn't believe that kind a places is exist . welldone sri lanka

title: Just when you think what is so special!
body: What a find, this is beautifully laid out and takes gardens to a new level, meandering walks, cool breezes, shady oasis and plenty of places to simply stop and smell the air.

title: Big Enough
body: Its big enough that you can feel you are in a hollywood movie where you are sent to a new planet and you have special house for each flowers species. No word and describe the beauty nor pictures can show you how beautiful this planet is.

title: 10 STARS!
body: Wow...what a collection of plants.I've never been to Kews Garden but believe that this botanical gardens is on par.We were very much overwhelmed the collection here.We spent 5 hours but suggest to spend the day here.Long walks to experience the beauty of this place. It was very eye opening.A must visit place for all botanist!

title: A beautiful botanical garden
body: We had a relaxing time at the Botanical Gardens in Kandy. This is a must visit place if you love Orchid flowers.

title: Good place to walk
body: The Royal Botanical Gardens at Peradeniya, near Kandy, is worth a visit if you have the time and fancy an interesting walk. There are some majestic old trees and a good orchid house.

title: Huge open spaces- interesting and well worth it
body: Beautiful location... nice stroll around in this beautiful garden- interesting watching the monkeys interacting.... nice time filler

title: Something for everyone
body: There is a great diversity of plants in the gardens. They are well laid out and maintained. The plan is clear if you want to follow a route and not miss anything, but it would be fine to just wander and enjoy the atmosphere. You do not need to be a keen gardener to enjoy this place.

title: Nature at its best
body: Must visit place. Flowers grass Trees . Everything is living. prepare yourself for long walk. Carry umbrella and water. Must do lunch in Botanic garden canteen. Don't forget to charge your camera or mobile you will be taking lot of photos.

title: Worth for Nuwaraeliya
body: its worth for your money to visit this beautiful garden. It was highly recommnded by our tour company shanew sri lanka tours.lots of varities of nice plants ,flowers and trees.beautiful landscaping.

title: Park
body: This is a must if you are here.The garden is beautifully laid out.A very good selection of plants.You can spend couple of hours here..

title: unexpected treasure in the middle of the city
body: We quite enjoyed the garden, which is well laid out, quite complete and incredibly maintained. Of particular interest is the orchid display, the medicinal garden and the beautiful annual walkway. Having been to a number of botanical gardens in the past all over the world, this one stands out for the attention to detail combined with a great maintenance practices. It rivals the Singapore Botanical Garden in its diversity and size. What also was impressive was the number of locals coming to visit and enjoy the space. Well worth the visit.

title: A Must-See especially for Nature Lovers
body: One of the few gardens in the whole world that got the balance right - natural vs human-intervened, old vs new, flurry of colours vs shades of green, tight spaces vs vast plains, etc. The giant century-old trees mesmerised me. I could have spend the whole day there absorbing the sights, sounds and fragrance if only there were more F&B outlets within the premise.

title: Round trip Sri Lanka
body: Nice park to be visited if you are in Kandy, good walking gear and some sun protection. Nice collection of different botanical species. Not to commercial.

title: A pleasant place to spend a day.
body: The herbs garden is relatively small but there are so many to see when you are wandering around with lush vegetation. Love the big lawn.

title: Walking through big giant trees
body: If u staying in Kandy do not miss this place it’s very beautiful when u went inside u will see a giant park with many varieties of flowers and giant tress it’s a large area to walk the big giant tress gives u some shades.If u’re going with ur girlfriend,wife or with daughters they will be more happy after seeing the beautiful flowers in the whole garden Good nice place.

title: Wonderful
body: The garden is located in the Kandy city center and it is kind of MUST SEE. It is a typical English style garden. Variety of tries, shrubs and flowers. You can see also monkies and big bats - they are active during the day. You need 3 hours to stay there. If tired there is a place to have a rest with soft drink, cofee or eat lunch.

title: Beautifull experience and a fantastic lay out
body: Do not miss this opportunity eventhough you are not into botanic ... it is a wonderfull place to visit and very relaxing ..... we took our time just to stroll around and saw orchids, spices, bamboo, variety of palm trees etc etc. fantastic.....

title: St Benedict's Monastery
body: St Benedict's is located in the Adisham bungalow and was built in 1913,which is named after Adisham a city in the English country of Kent.

title: Historical visit
body: What a place!Had a fabulous time with my aunt and uncle walking around on my birthday. The amount of exhibitions and knowledge you can acquire from a place like this is astonishing.I'd recommend you visit this not in one go as you will be absolutely exhausted as you have to walk alot . You should attempt to visit it in probably 3 days if you want to actually learn anything.Architecturally speaking, it is fantastic, just shows how great the buildings of old were. Being around for over 100 years and still holding all its glory, really amazes me.A lot to learn from this place I cannot wait to come back more times and check the new exhibitions.

title: Adisham Bunglaw
body: Adisham Bunglaw was built in 1931 by an English aristocrat and planter Sir Thomas Villiers.Beautiful place with fresh environment not any dust fresh air and tree 🌲 Amazing architecture and Wonderful history.Do come here if you are in Haputale.

title: Definitely worth a visit
body: Did you know that this breathtaking Tudor styled monastery was the famous Adisham Bungalow built in 1931 by Sir Thomas Lister Villers, an English planter? Therefore, leaving Good Fridays and Xmas apart, this 10 acre land is available for viewing on weekends and approx. Another 23 Sri Lankan public holidays a year!The Benedictine fathers are well known for cultivating and producing their very own line of natural Adisham fruit jams, jellies, cordials and chutneys. Gains from these fruitful jars of joy are utilized towards the maintenance of this beautiful 90 year old Tudor styled stone structure from the British era.

title: Closed on Weekdays
body: We went to this so called bungalow after our journey in nuwareliya, it was a very long Drive but unfortunately it's closed On weedays, someone at the gate said they only open on weekends and Public Holidays.We had to wait a long time at the gate because no one was there we wanted to know why it's closed.The Instructions voards on the gate say nothing about closing on weekdays.

title: Must visit this place.
body: This is a beautiful monastery with a rich history. Make sure to check the opening hours before going there.

title: A quick half hour tour
body: Beautiful setting, many areas kept in the same old setting and actual furniture of that time. Read up about the adisham history before you arrive. You can also book rooms here and stay overnight; but they are pretty much booked whole year round - very popular place

title: Don't visit
body: You can't see anything rather than garden.. it's always closed for guest you only can see outside and not allowed to go inside

title: A Little bit of England
body: A charming bit of England in exotic Sri Lanka. Worth a visit to see this lovely old structure. Sweet gardens and nic old books in the library.

title: " Visit to local England"
body: That was the ancient banglow built by British and now there is a monastery. The owners maintain it very well and there were many kinds of flowers. At the first visit I feel that I was in the UK.

title: A quick visit to the UK
body: One who goes to Haputale should definitely go here. It’s an ancient banglow built by a British. One who visits would feel like in the UK when you are there. It has a great piece of information about its history. Very interesting. So much detailing. You would just stare and this banglow and enjoy it’s beauty.

title: Beautiful grounds
body: A beautiful building and grounds with a nice flower garden, but inside was not as good. Maybe as it is a British building we had higher hopes for the interior.

title: Good place with history...
body: Good place to visit with historical background. It is a religious place. Only limited access is allowed.

title: Beautiful Nature Walk
body: I walked to the Monastery from my BnB, which was about a 2km walk uphill - I cannot recommend this enough - it was gorgeous. I didn't actually pay to enter because I did not bring any money with me but the hike itself was incredible and high recommended.

title: Building looks impressive as you approach but that is where it ends.
body: The 2 rooms on show were in poor condition with rising damp. They held minimal interest for us. We bought some mango jam which is quite nice

title: benedictine monastery
body: sir thomas lester villiers to recreate his English lifestyle he developed some english country-cottage

title: Not really worth it
body: It's a Nice monastry, but you can see very little of it. You can see 2 rooms only during the weekend. It's a bit small as welll.

title: Little to see
body: There is really little to see here. Three rooms of the house and a small part of the garden. Quite disappointing.

title: Great location to experience wild life in Sri Lanka
body: Wilpattu is one of the largest and most prominent national parks in Sri Lanka. The specialty of this park is that it contains over 100 natural lakes that spreads across a land of about 1300 square kilometers. The name Wilpattu has been derived by combining the terms "Willu (lakes)" and Pattu (land). This is located 185km from Colombo, just before Mannar. The park was closed until 2003 due to the Civil War and as of today, it is a highly valued wild life destination for both local and foreign tourists.

title: Tropical Not a British Stately Home, but that is the charm.
body: Our driver recommended this garden & house and we were not disappointed. The gardens, started in 1928, have a huge variety of tropical plants and trees. They are presented in formal & non-formal settings and provide a beautiful walk, shaded by these huge natural structures. It's not an immaculately kept stately home in Britain, this is Sri Lanka and not enough gardeners to keep up, but that is part of the charm of this place. The house and it's history are fascinating and has been visited by many famous people including Edward VII, Vivienne Lee and the Danish Queen Mother. We were treated to a lovely cup of local tea in the garden by the house. We were the only visitors at the time and enjoyed the tranquility of this hidden gem.

title: Architecture & Engineering Marvel......
body: Demodara loop, also known as the the spiral railway is recognised as one of the most fascinating civil engineering marvels in Sri Lanka. It is definitely one of the perfect spots for stunning pictures. The rail line passes under itself, going around the loop and emerging from a tunnel, which runs directly beneath the Demodara railway station. The rail loop is approximately 900 metres long and the tunnel is 320 metres in length. title: A Tourist Site?
body: The Jaffna Public Library is advertised as one of the sights to see in Northern Sri Lanka, During the civil war the Library which was even then one of the hallmarks of Jaffna was burnt down and now rebuilt. I had sent some books to Jaffna for the library, so I looked forward to seeing it.I went on a Sunday morning and was told it was closed, so I made an arrangement, after a conversation with the man at the gate, to come in early the next morning. I arrived at 9am and was told that visitors were allowed only after 4pm. I explained to the only one who could speak in English that I was from Australia, and that I had an interest in seeing the complex. I still had the same reply. In the end they let me through but showed no interest in my appearance there. I did not see all of it to make any comment. I felt that I was being treated as a inconvenience to be tolerated, and so I left.If you advertise something as a tourist attraction the you should make arrangements to make sure your visitors are made welcome.I do not think I will go back there and while I wish them success I will not personally contribute.

title: A must visit site in Jaffna
body: Nilavarai Well, also known as the "Bottomless Well" is one of the most famous sites in Jaffna. Its called "bottomless" because it has water throughout the year and does not dry up even during droughts. An interesting fact about this is that water within the first 40 feet is fresh which turns saline thereafter. This well has fascinating legends attached to it, where most of them tracing to the "Ramayanaya". The interesting history of this place and its uniqueness makes it absolutely worth the visit. Something diverse and unbelievable!
